# 03 Python to JavaScript to HTML

This is the key tutorial: **Python generates structured data, JavaScript reads it, and JavaScript returns HTML for display.**

That means you can use Python for data shaping and JS for presentation.

products = [
    {'name': 'Alpha Sensor', 'units': 18, 'target': 12},
    {'name': 'Beta Beacon', 'units': 9, 'target': 14},
    {'name': 'Gamma Relay', 'units': 21, 'target': 16},
    {'name': 'Delta Node', 'units': 13, 'target': 13},
]
for item in products:
    item['difference'] = item['units'] - item['target']
    item['status'] = 'ahead' if item['difference'] > 0 else ('behind' if item['difference'] < 0 else 'on target')

summary = {
    'total_units': sum(item['units'] for item in products),
    'ahead_count': sum(1 for item in products if item['status'] == 'ahead'),
    'behind_count': sum(1 for item in products if item['status'] == 'behind'),
}

nb['product_report'] = {
    'products': products,
    'summary': summary,
    'title': 'Production Snapshot'
}
print('Python stored product_report for JavaScript to render')
summary

const report = nb.get('product_report'); const products = report.products; const cards = products.map(item => { const color = item.status === 'ahead' ? '#16a34a' : item.status === 'behind' ? '#dc2626' : '#2563eb'; return `
${item.name} ${item.status}
Units: ${item.units} / Target: ${item.target}
Difference: ${item.difference}
`; }).join(''); return `

${report.title}

Python generated the data, JavaScript generated this HTML dashboard.

Total units: ${report.summary.total_units}
Ahead: ${report.summary.ahead_count}
Behind: ${report.summary.behind_count}
${cards}
`;

## Why this matters

This pattern is the bridge to richer notebook apps:

- Python handles calculation, transformation, and data shaping
- JavaScript handles rendering and browser-native presentation
- HTML becomes an output format, not just a separate hand-written cell

That is enough to build dashboards, inspectors, report cards, previews, and lightweight tools inside one notebook.

const report = nb.get('product_report');
return report.products.map(p => ({ name: p.name, status: p.status, difference: p.difference }));

## Try this next

- Edit the Python `products` list
- Change targets or add a new product
- Re-run the Python cell, then the JS rendering cell
- Watch the HTML dashboard update from Python-authored data
